body:
Review pass 25. bd-01KZXQAW39E8XCXJJVW7C7M2M6 closed - thanks. Both of my outstanding recommendations were adopted, and I checked them rather than assuming.

EPIC 6 MC TOLERANCE - pinned exactly as suggested, plus the variance bound:
  expected_standard_errors <- c(null = 0.0058, signal = 0.0119)
  4-sigma gates on the means AND expect_lte(observed se, 1.5 * expected) on both arms
It passes - 32 expectations, 0 failures - so the values I supplied from my base-R replication are compatible with your actual implementation, which was worth confirming since I produced them elsewhere. The test now fails for bias AND for variance inflation, which is what the acceptance wording asks for.

EPIC 7 PROVENANCE - the machinery is very good. metric_training_policy("exclude_evaluation") versus "all_partitions_residual_orthogonality" with an explicit justification string that itself records "metric uncertainty remains uncalibrated". Plans differ in signature and metric_schedule signature, and training_partitions is recorded per edge - "run3" for disjoint, c("run1","run2","run3") for all-runs. Values checked against learned_crossnobis_oracle at 5e-10. That is exactly the frozen-provenance contract, made observable.

What is not there yet is the statistical arm - a Monte Carlo comparison of the two policies with an equivalence margin. Epic 7 is still in flight so this may be coming; the reference numbers and the margin argument are in my decision note on that bead, and the headline is that I found no detectable leakage (paired z <= 0.83 at 500 reps), so the expected result is equivalence, which needs a margin rather than a null result.

ONE NUANCE, noted on Epic 9 rather than filed. The MC test runs under a fixed set.seed(8403), so it is deterministic - one realization, not a sampling statement. The variance bound still does real work, since a genuine variance inflation would show at that seed too. But if Epic 9 certifies "null estimates centre at zero across Monte Carlo replications", that currently rests on a single seed. Cheap fix: repeat the block over two or three fixed seeds. Otherwise phrase the certification as a reproducibility guard rather than a Monte Carlo result.

No new defects this pass.
